overview.description: Boston is an 18th-century French trick-taking game that represents a pivotal transition from Whist to modern Bridge. Played by four individuals with a standard 52-card deck, it introduced a sophisticated bidding system where players compete for contracts ranging from winning a few tricks to 'Misère' (winning none) or 'Grand Slam' (winning all). It is famous for its complex scoring tables and the use of two decks to track game state, embodying the intellectual rigor of Enlightenment-era social card play.

history.origins: Despite its name, Boston likely originated in France during the American Revolutionary War (circa 1770s), named in honor of the siege of Boston. It was a favorite of French naval officers and rapidly spread to the United States and across Europe.
timeline: 1770s: Boston emerges in French salons as a 'revolutionary' Whist variant.
1800s: Becomes extremely popular in the United States and Russia (featured in Tolstoy's 'War and Peace').
1900s: Superseded by Auction Bridge but survives in traditional clubs.
Present: A rare specialty game played by card game historians and historical reenactors.
history.evolution: Boston was the first major game to introduce a full hierarchy of contracts (bids), a concept that would later become the core of Bridge. It also introduced the idea of 'Misère' bids into the Whist family.
history.cultural: Portrayed in 19th-century literature as the game of the intellectual and social elite. Its complexity reflected the high-stakes diplomacy of the era.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card French pack. Two packs are often used: one for play and one for determining trump rotation.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, extensive scoring counters (fiches), and a specific Boston score table.
setup.dealing: Deal 13 cards to each player (usually in batches of 4-4-5).

rules.objective: Win tricks according to the level of the declared contract. Higher contracts pay more but carry greater penalties.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid for contracts (e.g., 'Boston' for 8 tricks, 'Petit Misère' for zero). 2. **Trump**: The suit of the turned-up card from the second deck usually determines the 'preference' suit for trumps. 3. **The Play**: Standard trick-taking rules. Must follow suit. 4. **Tricks**: Highest trump wins; else highest card of led suit wins.
keyRules: Preference Suit: One suit (usually Diamonds) is the 'Preference' and outranks other suits in the auction.
Misère: A contract to lose every trick; there are no trumps in Misère hands.
Independence: Unlike Whist, you usually play alone against the other three defenders.

strategy.basic: Evaluate your hand for both high-trick potential and low-trick potential. A hand with many 7s and 8s is perfect for a Misère bid.
strategy.intermediate: Auction Tactics: Use the 'Preference' suit to overcall opponents even if your trick count is lower. Knowing when to 'Double' an opponent's contract is key to defensive scoring.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Coordination: Since three players defend against one declarer, they must cooperate to force the declarer to win (in Misère) or lose (in Boston) tricks. Lead through the declarer to trap their high cards.
tips: Don't bid Boston (8 tricks) without at least four solid trumps and an Ace in a side suit.
Watch the 'Independence' bids carefully—they are the highest-scoring and highest-risk plays.

difficulty.easy: Bids only on trick count. Follows suit legally. Does not understand Misère strategy.
difficulty.medium: Evaluates hand for all contract types. Understands suit preference in the auction. Basic defensive coordination.
difficulty.hard: Optimal contract selection using Monte Carlo simulations. Perfectly coordinates defense against the declarer. Expert at 'throwing' tricks in Misère rounds.

considerations: Requires a multi-contract evaluation engine (High vs. Low goals).
Defense logic must handle 3-vs-1 asymmetric cooperation.

additional: Tolstoy, Leo. War and Peace. (References to the game)

ante.reason: Boston is a point-based trick-taking game and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante system.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of thirteen cards to each player is handled automatically by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: This is a closed-hand bidding game where all cards are dealt; no community market or shared cards exist.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase or swap cards from any external area; they must play with their original hand.

buy_stock.reason: The entire deck is distributed at the start of the round; no cards remain in stock to be purchased.

fold.reason: Participation is mandatory for every trick to determine if the declarer meets their bid requirement.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking and bidding structure rather than a vying structure where checking would apply.

call.reason: There is no bet to match in this game; competition is based on contract levels and trick wins.

bet.reason: Success is measured by points on a complex scoring table rather than through direct financial betting.

raise.reason: Contract levels are increased during the auction phase via bidding rather than through wagering rounds.

declare.reason: The auction result defines the contract; no separate declaration phase exists during the actual card play.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands stay private until cards are played into tricks; no full-hand reveal phase occurs in the game.

award_pot.reason: Winning points are calculated based on the scoring table and awarded from other players rather than a pot.

play_card.description: Play a card from your hand to the current trick following suit rules.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit; highest trump or highest led card wins.

draw.reason: Each player receives thirteen cards at the start and no further drawing occurs during the play phase.

discard.reason: Every card in the hand must be played into a trick; no cards are discarded to a waste pile.

pass.description: Pass during the auction when not wishing to bid a higher contract.
pass.constraints: Allowed at any time during the bidding phase.

bid.description: Submit a contract bid consisting of a trick count and a suit (or Misère).
bid.constraints: Must exceed the current bid in the hierarchy of contracts.

meld.reason: Boston is a trick-taking game based on counts rather than forming sequences or melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates automatically once all thirteen tricks have been played by all participants.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: The hand size is fixed at 13; no draw pile exists during the trick-taking play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played directly to tricks; no separate waste or discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit values to tricks; no card has a secondary engine action.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Bidding is performed openly clockwise; no hidden declaration tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Boston is a trick-taking game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: Points are earned strictly through trick counting; no melding of card sets is part of the gameplay.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: None; highest card of lead suit or highest trump wins the trick.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Highest bidder leads the first trick.

customActions.description: Distribute thirteen cards to each of the four players.
Place a bid for a specific number of tricks and a trump suit choice.
customActions.constraints: Must be higher than the previous bid in the contract table.

customActions.description: Determine point transfers based on the declarer's success or failure.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card rank comparison determines trick winner (Ace is high).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for Boston (Preference family) where diamonds are often the preference suit and bidding determines the contract.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). In Boston, diamonds often have preference (higher bid value); trump is chosen by the winning bidder. Follow suit when able; standard trick order applies.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit: ace high, then king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two low. Standard trick-taking order; the contract and declarer's goal (e.g. no tricks lost) follow Boston rules.
engine.dealPattern: Individually clockwise until hand is full.

hero.title: BOSTON
hero.subtitle: The Enlightenment Duel
hero.tagline: Bid the siege. Hold the line. Outwit the three.

synthesis.shortDescription: The missing link between Whist and Bridge. Boston is a masterful game of individual skill where you bid for contracts against three defending rivals. Whether chasing a Grand Slam or hiding in a Misère, the psychological battle of the auction is where the true game is won.

prompts.human: You have a hand full of low cards but the Ace of Diamonds (Preference). Do you bid a small Boston, or risk a 'Petit Misère' to lose every single trick?
prompts.ai: Game: Boston. Type: Auction Trick-taking. Rules: 4 individuals. 52 cards. Bid determines contract (High tricks vs Misère). Diamonds are Preference. Declarer vs 3 Defenders.

scoring.description: Scoring is performed via a detailed table matching bid level to result. Losers pay declarer, or declarer pays each defender.
scoring.winCondition: Highest point total after a set number of hands.

penalties.Failed Boston: Declarer pays a heavy penalty to every defender based on the number of tricks missed.

scoring.splitRules: None; only one winner per hand.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by hand count.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards contribute to trick wins rather than having point values.
